training.transport_scope: Complete archive reconstructed from supplied index and both split parts. No uploaded code executed or checkpoints deserialized in this review.
training.evidence_scope: Source matches repository commit 31a607b. Parent verified 152 native CUDA test cases at each of six GPU stages (912 repeated executions of the same 152 cases), and all 744 prepared references accepted with eight workers. Training observations below are recorded native CUDA results; aggregate loss is normalized one-step MSE plus 0.5 two-step MSE, not RMS or maximum error.
interpretation: Classical diffusion-first orientation accounts for the dominant 23.7-fold validation-loss reduction; it is not neural novelty.

RF source transport plus nonlinear-time decoding improves the one-seed minimal controls, but the optimized source family slightly surpasses optimized source_time. Nonlinear time is not uniformly beneficial.
Only 4.65% best RF validation loss reduction from source_closure and initialization-selected default closure do not support keeping current closure as primary path.

All 18 matched compression trials and all 4 conditional kernel trials selected learned checkpoints. Source vs precompression and deep parameter-matched FNO each wins 2/3 paired validation seeds, without robust across-seed accuracy dominance.

Source has fewer transforms and measured 1.65-1.79-fold lower step cost than the deep parameter-matched FNO, while the one-layer equal-width FNO has similar or lower measured cost and often lower validation loss. Deep-FNO speed comparison does not establish an FNO-paper win.

Kernel rank2 with 120 parameters is best of four tested kernel variants on one validation seed and reduces DF-base normalized validation loss about 36.7%; extra transforms and independent confirmation remain decisive.
Parameter count is not total runtime: rank2 uses 9 correction transforms plus 4 base transforms; source uses 2+4; matched-depth4 FNO uses 8+4.
No numerical gradient failure is apparent, clipping is rare, and many selected checkpoints precede the final update. More indiscriminate training is unsupported.
Downstream DF models inherited learning rate and batch size optimized on RF; optimize the actual chosen DF orientation in a new development protocol.
Compressed encoder still has a full physical-source and base bypass; the experiment does not isolate a complete information bottleneck.
Trial identifiers say reaction-first/b1 even when effective recorded model uses diffusion-first/b8; use explicit trial metadata for labeling and comparison.

The full confirmation source_time control selected the diffusion-first initialization and source_closure selected the reaction-first initialization; confirmation therefore cannot establish benefit from a trained nonlinear time decoder or trained closure. Both outcomes remain explicit.
bounded_next_directions: Correct orientation/configuration labels and tune the chosen diffusion-first base with paired short update budgets and a new development cohort.
Keep source and rank2 kernels; pause the current closure pending separate mean/spatial error analysis.
Replicate rank2 across all three paired seeds and include rank1 and zero-weight controls before widening rank.
Add the cheaper one-layer source-constrained FNO to future held-out comparisons as well as the deep parameter-matched FNO.
Inspect physical residual-aligned loss and per-regime decomposition without changing success gates retrospectively; retain targets and current confirmations as inspected development evidence.

confirmation.scope: read-only independent recomputation from complete uploaded JSON; no uploaded executable run or fresh reference tensor inspected; artifact closure independently handled by parent

paired_design.interpretation: Rows across shared parents, grids, seeds, schedules and targets are paired observations; no independent-sample/population claim. Inspected full cohort now development for subsequent architecture selection; a new confirmation must use new disjoint parents/IDs.

caveats: Reported accuracy coverage is reference-informed post-hoc schedule frontier, not accuracy of every queried schedule nor a deployable step selector.
Two descriptive gate passes belong to initialization-selected source_time against GL3 alone; no trained joint gate pass.
Same-grid nodal-FD and dealiased continuum-estimate errors must remain separate. Near-identical continuum errors among methods suggest shared spatial-discretization bias dominates here.
Matched FNO comparator is project adaptation, not the published FNO paper or universal neural solver leaderboard.

acceptance_policies.scope: Read-only independent JSON audit. No uploaded code executed and no tensor payload unpickled. Local policy inner/outer files individually hash-checked; parent verified complete reconstructed eight-stage lineage separately.

calibration.independence_caveat: Cohorts disjoint by parent ID; paired grids/horizons/models/estimators are repeated observations. Full fresh bank is eight controlled continuous fields crossed with four physics settings, not independent random field draws.

cost_scope: Each endpoint includes all its own rejected proposals, estimator computations, accepted proposal and fallback cost. All cost recomputations agree.
Shared benchmark computes all estimator components; actual unique attempt-work is 635.782 seconds. Summed hypothetical policy charges reuse those components and are not actual elapsed stage time.
Both classical controls are fixed eightfold refinement of first proposal: 24 substeps at horizon .27, 72 at .81. They are not fastest feasible/tolerance-matched frontier selections.
Policy timing is one synchronized complete rollout sample, no warmup; no statistically established timing advantage.
Source step-doubling median ETDRK4 ratio .851 hides tails: cost total 6.168 vs 4.415 seconds, ratio1.397; wins139/192.
interpretation: All nine same-grid policy/model groups passed empirical false-acceptance check: 1179 accepted, zero false accepts,549 fallback, all1728 endpoint predictions satisfy both2e-4 targets.
FALSE_ACCEPTANCE_GATE_PASS is explicitly the discrete track only. It does not approve continuum deployment.
Continuum transfer has306 false accepts/410 accepted74.63%; all306 exceed target even after subtracting uncertainty, not just ambiguous upper bounds. All nine continuum groups fail.

Continuum teachers/classical controls have matching endpoint coverage126/432, with grid32:12.5%,64:18.75%,128:56.25%. This points to shared finite-difference-versus-continuum spatial target mismatch; policy only measures same-grid temporal defects.

Step doubling is the only policy mechanism with plausible small median cost advantage for source; source_time nearly neutral versusETDRK4. Flow residual JVP/combined envelope and moment-closure policies are much more expensive on this implementation.
No certificate, population false-accept bound, fastest-classical superiority, FNO policy superiority or independent replication established by these counts.
recommendations: Keep source+step doubling as practical pilot while retaining rejected-work tail cost and full fixed-control scope.

Build matched PDE/discretization target and independently calibrated spatial+temporal error estimate before any continuum-deployment claim. Compare spectral-base/exact symbol and consistent dealiased reaction against FD as controlled arms.
Benchmark fastest accuracy-matched classical frontiers and independently time deployed policy alone, retaining total/quantile/tail costs rather than median only.
Avoid expanding expensive JVP or variance closure work until measured cost/accuracy improves.

Q1.evidence: All finite-step mathematical controls completed; reversed unseen steps cause learned Source/FNO overshoot despite high reference-informed frontier coverage.
Q1.conclusion: Cubic/asymptotic structure and physical zero limits do not guarantee finite-step accuracy.

Q2.evidence: Stiff-scale controls passed; diffusion-first base dominates the minimal validation gain; phase/eigenvalue-conditioned rank2 is more robust than generic transported source on these recorded schedules.
Q2.conclusion: Retain coupled stiffness response, but isolate its benefit on cases with accuracy headroom over the chosen physical base.

Q3.evidence: Constructive rank4/8 gates pass, but learned rank2 has the best one-seed kernel validation result and strongest observed compact robustness.
Q3.conclusion: Constructive rank and trained nominal rank are different quantities; replicate low ranks with actual cost and phase-varied fresh fields.

Q4.evidence: Continuum accuracy is almost identical across classical/learned arms and improves roughly fourfold per resolution doubling; precompression comparisons are mixed and retain full-source/base bypasses.
Q4.conclusion: Shared spatial discretization bias dominates this continuum track; the information-bottleneck hypothesis remains unresolved.

Q5.evidence: All calibration envelopes and 4326 acceptance decisions independently match; zero discrete false accepts, but 306/410 accepted continuum endpoints fail their target.
Q5.conclusion: The discrete empirical estimator does not certify continuum error; spatial and temporal targets require a consistent calibration design.

Q6.evidence: Independent prescribed-schedule endpoints reveal reverse-order failures obscured by selecting a feasible schedule after observing reference errors.
Q6.conclusion: Report every queried schedule and step order, with worst cases, separately from the post-hoc work-precision frontier.

Q7.evidence: All 3147 rejected attempts are charged. Source+step-doubling median ETDRK4 ratio0.851 contrasts with total ratio1.397. The fixed-refined control is not the fastest accuracy-matched classical frontier.
Q7.conclusion: Retain total and tail cost, and independently time complete deployments against the cheapest accurate classical choice before claiming a solver benefit.
